boundaries.statement: The default warm-up contains exactly five question/answer pairs (10 slides). A different count is valid only when the current user explicitly requested it.
evidence: current request when count is overridden

boundaries.statement: Every question slide contains exactly three student tasks with literal labels ALL, MOST and SOME. It contains no WHY box, reasoning prompt, explanation prompt or fourth student task.
evidence: semantic review of the question slide

boundaries.statement: Every question slide is followed immediately by its matched answer slide. No reminder, transition, model, unrelated answer or other slide may appear between the pair.
Every answer slide preserves the ALL, MOST and SOME order and positions from the preceding question slide and supplies the matched answer for all three tasks.
evidence: semantic comparison of each adjacent question/answer pair

boundaries.statement: Reasoning or explanation appears on the answer slide only, in the established bottom green WHY panel. The answer-slide explanation is concise mathematical reasoning rather than a generic checking instruction.
evidence: semantic review of both slides in every pair

boundaries.statement: Every graph, chart or pictograph used in the warm-up exposes the key or unit interval needed to recover every exact answer; sparse scales that require guessing an unmarked exact value fail.
evidence: comparison of every graph question with the visible scale

boundaries.statement: Every meaningful ALL/MOST/SOME task or answer is at least 36 pt and the answer-slide WHY explanation is at least 28 pt.

Inspect every pair against the resolved context and prior-learning evidence or explicit candidate assumptions. All remains accessible and Most provides worthwhile secure retrieval; an accessible floor is not a ceiling for Most/Some. Do not claim actual attainment or taught knowledge without evidence.

For every pair name the mathematical demand Some adds beyond Most in the same focus. Larger numbers, extra steps or a task label alone are insufficient. Keep concise retrieval responses and do not add untaught procedures or additional compulsory explanation demands merely to create challenge.

Evaluate the three tasks together in every pair. A neighbouring tier must not give away the answer or collapse the intended demand into a trivial restatement. Useful inverse relationships or deliberate fluency remain valid when independently worthwhile and justified.

release_rule: Every applicable boundary requires explicit PASS evidence. A missing result or any FAIL makes the standalone component not component-ready and blocks whole-pack release when used inside Daily Lesson Pack.
